explanation: Theorem 1: a connected triangle-free graph with f = 2 (f the maximum multiplicity of a degree) is bipartite, has minimum degree 1, and has a compact degree sequence (d_{k+2} = d_k + 1). This matches the summary ('if no degree occurs more than twice, the graph is bipartite'). The connectivity hypothesis is needed for minimum degree 1: K₂ plus an isolated vertex has f = 2 but minimum degree 0. Source: Erdős–Fajtlowicz–Staton, 'Degree sequences in triangle-free graphs', Discrete Math. 92 (1991) 85–88. The full text was not accessible; the zbMATH review summary says that triangle-free graphs in which no degree occurs more than twice are bipartite, and that every triangle-free graph is an induced subgraph of one in which no degree occurs more than three times. Plausibly faithful; the full statement could not be checked against the paper.
